cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Can You Keep It?
cards.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club's changing the menu. Keep that quiet; I'll handle the announcement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't tell anyone. Can I still complain about the old one?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Complain all you like. The chef's leaving; don't let that slip while you do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'd better stop asking Sam who she wants cooking next season.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk to Sam. I'm taking over the kitchen; tell me what you've said before I tell you who's coming with me.

reason: Replace the undeveloped lock metaphor with progressively sensitive menu, chef and takeover details; B potential gossip triggers a concrete accounting test before A names the team, while A adjusts talk boundaries and handles Sam.
